We have reported a new ultra-fast, sensitive and robust method (2 min run time; >87% recovery; LOQ and LOD of 37–156 and 4–20 nmol L−1, respectively; and intra- and inter-day precision lower than 10%) with improved performance for the analysis of sulforaphane and their metabolites in human urine. The recorded data showed that the bioavailability of SFN reached up to 40%, being absent in the time-matched baseline urine. A new ultra-fast, accurate, robust, and selective UHPLC/MS/MS procedure (2-min chromatogram; >87% recovery; LOQ and LOD of 20–156 and 4–20 nmol L−1, respectively; and intra- and inter-day variations lower than 10%) was used for the simultaneous determination of GR and SFN in human urine. The analytical capacity of this novel method was further tested by determining the bioavailability of GR and its metabolic derivatives in urine from volunteers after the consumption of ½ and 1 servings of broccoli sprouts (30 and 60 g, respectively).
The aim of this work was the development of a fast, accurate, robust, and selective analytical method to determine the bioavailability of the most relevant bioactive compounds present in broccoli sprouts using solid phase extraction (SPE) as the extraction procedure and UHPLC/MS/MS, operating in multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) mode, as the analytical platform. The developed method was validated and further tested by determining the bioavailability of SFN and its metabolic derivatives in human urine after the ingestion of a single intake of ½ and 1 serving (60 g) of broccoli sprouts by healthy volunteers.
